title: Review: Forces and momentum

Terms and clues: A.2.10#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.2.12#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.2.11#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.2.15#xt1 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: The product of mass and velocity; its rate of change equals the resultant force.

items.label: Explosion
items.clue: An event in which internal forces push the parts of a system apart, often from rest.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: An impact in which the total kinetic energy of the bodies is the same before and after.

items.label: Centripetal force
items.clue: The resultant, directed radially inwards, that changes a body's direction but not its speed.

questions.stem: Two blocks, A of mass 5.0 kg and B of mass 7.0 kg, are in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal force of 60 N pushes block A, which in turn pushes block B, and both accelerate together. What is the magnitude of the force that A exerts on B?
questions.explanation: Treat A and B as one system: a = 60 N/12 kg = 5.0 m s⁻². On B's free-body diagram the only horizontal force is the push from A, so it equals m_B a = 7.0 kg × 5.0 m s⁻² = 35 N.

questions.stem: A block of mass 4.0 kg slides down a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal. The coefficient of dynamic friction between the block and the plane is 0.20. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the magnitude of the frictional force on the block?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular to the plane there is no acceleration, so F_N = mg cos 25° = 4.0 × 9.8 × 0.906 = 35.5 N. The block slides, so F_f = μ_d F_N = 0.20 × 35.5 N = 7.1 N.

questions.stem: Which statement about field forces is correct?

options.text: A magnetic field exerts a force on a charged particle even when it is at rest.
An electric field exerts a force on a charged particle even when it is at rest.
A gravitational force acts on a body only where there is air around it.
An astronaut in orbit has no weight, as gravity does not act there.

questions.explanation: An electric field exerts a force F_e on any charge in it, whether the charge is moving or stationary. This is one of the differences between the electric and the magnetic force.

questions.stem: Under which condition does the total momentum of a system of interacting bodies remain constant?

options.text: When every collision between the bodies is elastic
When the bodies exert no forces at all on one another
When no resultant external force acts on the system
When every body in the system moves at a constant speed

questions.explanation: Forces between the bodies are internal and cancel in third-law pairs, so only an external resultant force can change the total momentum. With no resultant external force, the total momentum is constant, whatever happens inside the system.

questions.stem: A cricket ball is struck by a bat. During the short time of contact the force between the bat and the ball rises from zero to a maximum and then falls back to zero. Which statement about the impulse delivered to the ball is correct?

options.text: It is the product of the maximum force exerted on the ball and the total time of contact.
It is the product of the average resultant force on the ball and the time of contact.
It is the largest value reached by the resultant force on the ball during the contact.
It is the average resultant force on the ball divided by the total time of contact.

questions.stem: A free-body diagram for a puck on a frictionless horizontal air table shows three horizontal forces: 30 N towards the east, 10 N towards the west and 15 N towards the north. The vertical forces on the puck balance. What is the magnitude of the resultant force on the puck?
questions.explanation: East–west: 30 N − 10 N = 20 N east. North: 15 N. These are perpendicular, so the resultant is √(20² + 15²) N = 25 N.

questions.stem: A solid steel sphere and a solid aluminium sphere have the same volume. Both hang from threads, completely under water: the steel sphere 0.20 m below the surface and the aluminium sphere 0.50 m below it. Steel is about three times as dense as aluminium. How do the buoyancy forces on the two spheres compare?

options.text: It is larger on the steel sphere, as steel is the denser metal
It is larger on the aluminium sphere, as that one is deeper
It is zero on both spheres, as neither sphere would float
They are equal, as each sphere displaces the same volume of water

questions.explanation: F_b = ρVg, where ρ is the density of the water and V is the volume displaced. Both spheres are fully immersed and have the same volume, so they displace equal volumes of the same fluid and experience equal buoyancy.

questions.stem: An astronaut has a mass of 70.0 kg on Earth, where g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹. She travels to the Moon, where g = 1.62 N kg⁻¹. Which statement about the astronaut on the Moon is correct?

options.text: Her weight is 686 N.
Her mass is reduced.
Her weight is 113 N.
Her weight is 0.0 N.

questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on location, so it stays 70.0 kg. Weight is F_g = mg = 70.0 kg × 1.62 N kg⁻¹ = 113 N.

questions.stem: A ball is released from rest and falls towards the ground. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about momentum during the fall is correct?

options.text: The ball's momentum increases, while the total momentum of the ball and the Earth stays constant.
The ball's momentum stays constant, because momentum is conserved in every situation.
The ball's momentum stays constant, because its gain in E_k equals its loss in E_p.
The ball's momentum increases, and the Earth's is unchanged, as the ball cannot pull it.

questions.stem: A crate on a rough horizontal floor is pushed horizontally with a constant force of 40.0 N for 5.00 s. Throughout this time the crate slides forwards and the dynamic frictional force on it is 15.0 N. What is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the crate by the resultant force during the 5.00 s?

options.text: 200 N s
125 N s
275 N s
5.0 N s

questions.explanation: The resultant force is 40.0 N − 15.0 N = 25.0 N forwards. The impulse of the resultant force is J = FΔt = 25.0 N × 5.00 s = 125 N s.

questions.stem: A small steel sphere of diameter 2.0 mm is released in a tall tube of glycerol and falls at terminal velocity. The weight of the sphere is 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ N and its volume is 4.2 × 10⁻⁹ m³. The density of glycerol is 1.3 × 10³ kg m⁻³ and its viscosity is 1.4 Pa s. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the terminal velocity of the sphere?

A crate of mass 12 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficients of friction between the crate and the floor are μ_s = 0.50 and μ_d = 0.40. A worker pushes horizontally on the crate with a force of 40 N, but the crate does not move. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the frictional force on the crate?

options.text: 40 N, equal and opposite to the worker's push
59 N, which is the value of μ_s F_N for the crate
47 N, the value of μ_d F_N for the crate
0 N, as friction acts only when a crate slides

questions.explanation: F_N = mg = 118 N, so the maximum static friction is μ_s F_N = 59 N. The 40 N push is less than this, so the crate stays at rest, and equilibrium requires friction of 40 N opposite to the push: F_f ≤ μ_s F_N is an inequality.
